NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by ifie, to 
investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of employees,or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
In performing its functions under this 
order the board shall comply with the 
requirements of section 502 of the De­
fense i Production Act of 1950, as 
amended.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Northwest Airlines, Inc., or 
its employees in the conditions out of 
which the said dispute arose.

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10319 (17 FR 188; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10319 and signed January 4, 1952. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between Northwest Airlines, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by the International Association of Machinists, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order, and a sentence requiring the board to comply with section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline, the non-derogation sentence and the Defense Production Act compliance sentence and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10319 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a airline labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The machine dossier did not locate the revoking provision for this pair; the held text of EO 12553 does contain the row for this order (number followed by a subject line) in the No. Subject table on its page 10, and the enacting sentence precedes the table, so the whole held EO 12553 text is cited as the ending source. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed. The sentence requiring compliance with section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950 is a condition on how the board performs its functions; the statute is not held in this repository, so no expiry of that statute is shown and none is claimed as an earlier end.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute. The Defense Production Act compliance sentence is a condition on the board's performance, not a separate command with its own sunset shown in held evidence.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects: the held text of EO 12553 contains no savings or exception clause attached to the revocation list (the enacting provision is a single sentence followed by the table, and the only effective-date or exception wording found anywhere in the order is outside it). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; no held source shows any continuing independent effect.","scope_check":"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. The order has no amendment in the held corpus."}
